annotationRationale: The main route reduces the spatial angle to a triangle with known sides. The projection alternative supplies a useful route through centroid ratios and right-triangle trigonometry.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: With edge length 2, CM=DM=√3 and CD=2, giving cos(∠CMD)=1/3, choice B. The statement, choices, key and supplied source figure are consistent. No grading conflict appears.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods are supplied. The LIVE argument and Random Math second solution are retained in cosine-law-section; Random Math first solution is retained in project-to-face-center. The existing vector route would repeat the same metric calculation with additional notation, so another method is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed cosine-law concept accurately describes the primary route, and Pythagoras is supporting knowledge in both methods. The projection alternative records its different central concepts directly. No contextual annotation is needed.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The isosceles-face median is an altitude, so CM²=DM²=4−1=3. Matching CD with the angle at M gives (3+3−4)/(2√3√3)=1/3. All lengths and the included angle are matched correctly.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately credits the LIVE explanation and Random Math second solution as third-party sources using source-informed-original. The prose independently explains the standard calculation. Random Math's footer does not establish official MAA authorship, and none is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why the midpoint is useful. The altitude, right-triangle calculation and opposite-side identification make every decisive transition reconstructible without another diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_137 supports the median-altitude property, cnm_174 supplies the face lengths, and math:general-cosine-law-application exactly covers recovery of the desired cosine. All three immediate nodes are appropriate.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for isosceles-triangle properties and Pythagoras fit the supporting steps. No accepted CN link is supplied for the local general cosine-law node.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.7 supports the right-triangle lengths; G-CO.C.10 supports the triangle-property context. G-SRT.D.10 and D.11 provide partial cosine-law alignment: this method applies the law but does not prove both laws or use the sine law.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate concepts precisely cover the written derivation, including its central cosine-law application.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Pythagoras gives OA=OB=OC, locating the projection at the circumcenter and hence centroid of the equilateral face. Thus MO=MC/3. Since MD=MC and DO⊥MO, the coincident rays MO and MC give cos(∠CMD)=MO/MD=1/3.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits Random Math first solution as nonofficial, source-informed work. The candidate supplies an independent justification for the projection's location, which the reference states without proof.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The circumcenter-to-centroid transition, orientation of the 2:1 ratio, equality of face medians and right-triangle cosine are all explained. The argument is complete using words alone.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five immediate nodes are used: Pythagoras, circumcenter, centroid ratios, acute-angle cosine and line-plane perpendicularity. The spatial conclusion follows from explicitly stated elementary facts.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for Pythagoras, circumcenter and acute-angle trigonometric definitions fit. No accepted CN links are supplied for the two local centroid/perpendicularity concepts.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.7 and G-SRT.C.6 support the length and cosine steps. G-C.A.3 provides partial circumcircle context. G-CO.C.10 names median concurrency but does not explicitly specify the 2:1 metric ratio; spatial perpendicularity also remains outside the supplied links.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct mapping captures this route's central projection and centroid reasoning without substituting the cosine-law node.
